correctness.rationale: Stationarity against arbitrary antiderivatives of \(x\) gives \(\mathbb E[v\mid x]=0\). Applying the generator to \(\phi(x)v\) then removes the nonlinear damping term conditionally and yields \(\mathbb E[\phi'(x)v^2]=\mathbb E[x\phi(x)]\). In distribution form this is \(\eta'=-x\rho\); the compactly supported tail first moment \(q(x)=\int_{[x,\infty)}s\rho(ds)\) has the same derivative, and finiteness removes the constant-Lebesgue ambiguity, proving \(\eta=qdx\). Monomial tests give the moment hierarchy. The exact mechanical-energy derivative gives \(\mathbb E[(1-x^2)v^2]=0\), which with the \(k=0,2\) hierarchy identities gives \(\mathbb E[x^4]=3\mathbb E[x^2]\). Cauchy–Schwarz and invariance exclude the nonzero endpoint \(\mathbb E[x^2]=3\). The packaged checker verifies the critical polynomial identities from its actual package path.

value.rationale: The result is a structural characterization of how kinetic energy is distributed across position in the canonical van der Pol self-oscillator. Rather than bounding one chosen orbit average, it determines the entire position projection of \(v^2d\pi\) from the position marginal for every compact stationary state. The resulting infinite hierarchy collapses the nonlinear damping balance to the parameter-independent exact law \(\mathbb E[x^4]=3\mathbb E[x^2]\), yielding a universal strict RMS ceiling and proving that any recurrent oscillation must carry kinetic energy through both the amplifying and dissipating sides of the nonlinear damping. These are reusable consistency checks for stationary or periodic data and are not a routine recomputation of the known limit cycle.
